title.en: Surface Area and Volume of Cylinder, Cone and Sphere

text.en: A water tank is a cylinder, an ice-cream cone is a cone, and a football is a sphere. To paint the tank or fill the cone we need surface area and volume formulas.

Surface area is the area of the outside of a solid and is measured in square units. Volume is the space inside and is measured in cubic units. We use π = 22/7 unless told otherwise.
For a cylinder of radius r and height h the curved surface area is 2πrh, the total surface area is 2πr(r + h) and the volume is πr²h.
For a cone of radius r, height h and slant height l, we have l² = r² + h². The curved surface area is πrl, the total surface area is πr(l + r) and the volume is one third of πr²h.
For a sphere of radius r, the surface area is 4πr² and the volume is four thirds of πr³. A hemisphere has curved surface area 2πr², total surface area 3πr² and volume two thirds of πr³.

problem.en: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Use π = 22/7.

prompt.en: A friend says Volume of a cone is πr²h, the same as a cylinder. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: A cone fits inside a cylinder of the same base and height
Three cones of water fill that cylinder
So the cone volume is one third of πr²h

points.en: Cone: CSA πrl and volume one third of πr²h.
Sphere: area 4πr² and volume four thirds of πr³.
